title: External credential vault and integration gating
goal: Remove plaintext external credentials and keep every unverified provider disabled until encrypted lifecycle verification passes

in: Social OAuth credential persistence, migration or revocation, encryption, rotation, refresh, disconnect, logging, and provider gating
out: Enabling providers before credential and lifecycle acceptance passes

acceptance_criteria: No plaintext access or refresh token is persisted or emitted to logs
Existing plaintext credentials are migrated safely or revoked with recorded disposition
Encrypted store, rotation, refresh, disconnect, and log-redaction tests pass
Social OAuth and other unverified providers remain disabled until their acceptance evidence is recorded

Reworked lib/integrations/token-vault.ts into an encrypted-only boundary: writes never touch legacy venue_social_integrations plaintext columns (dual-write retired), reads fail closed (legacy key_version=0 copies, tampered or wrong-key envelopes, and malformed bytes resolve to null — never to raw token text), server-only key access retained, and audit metadata is redacted through redactCredentialLog before persistence.

Organization social OAuth callback now persists encrypted envelopes only (buildOrganizationCredentialPayload) and fails the connect when encryption fails instead of degrading to plaintext persistence.

Authored additive forward-only migration supabase/migrations/20260921000000_intg007_encrypted_social_credential_vault.sql (SUPABASE_TELEMETRY off, superset of the active chain, planned manifest in docs/engineering/migration-validation/) revoking client column SELECT on organization_social_integrations.access_token/refresh_token and revoking legacy plaintext copies (org + venue source columns and key_version=0 vault bytes). NOT applied — CP-051 manual apply is hosted and out of scope.
